jobs.title: Environmental Scientist 1 - Jackson, TN/Hybrid
jobs.description:
Environmental Scientist 1

Jackson, TN/Hybrid

12+ Months

We are seeking a candidate who has practices excellent customer service and can effectively communicate with a diverse internal and external customer base. Preferred candidates will possess strong time management, and organizational skills. The position requires fieldwork in rural areas, construction sites, and in all weather conditions, and frequent day travel. Preferred bachelor’s degrees include environmental science, biology, chemistry, wildlife biology, or related. Preference may be given to candidates with a background in chemical sampling, microbenthic invertebrate sampling and identification, and laboratory analyses and procedures of water samples.

General Responsibilities Include

Collecting chemical, bacteriological and biological samples of surface waters for analysis to assess stream health.
Conduct sanitary surveys of community and non-community public water systems to ensure compliance with federal and state drinking water standards.
Serve as a knowledgeable point of contact for public water system operators, landowners, and local stakeholders, providing guidance on regulatory requirements and compliance.
Travel regularly to monitoring sites and public water systems across a 17-county service area using a state-provided vehicle.
Accurately document field findings, maintain organized records, and input data into digital systems.
Participate in occasional investigations related to illegal discharges, surface water quality concerns, or public water drinking water complaints.
Collaborate with internal regulatory teams, consultants, water system operators, elected officials, and members of the public to resolve issues and support environmental goals.

jobs.title: Water Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental Studies SpecialistUnder direct supervision, this position conducts environmental studies of designated ecological resources, including wetlands, forests, streams, soils, plants, and wildlife, in order to identify and evaluate any potential impacts to these resources in and near Department project sites. It also monitors compliance with local, state, and federal regulations during all phases of Department work.Examples of WorkConduct site investigations, data collection, and plan reviews to determine potential project impacts.Apply procedures, laws, standards, and regulations pertaining to compliance with the Clean Water Act (CWA) and/or Section 7 of the Endangered Species Act (ESA).Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies to secure any necessary concurrence/permits.Assist in collecting, analyzing, and summarizing ecological resources to support National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and project development activities.Develop and maintain project records to document and track compliance with permits and regulations.Prepare project documents, such as constraints statements, coordination letters, special provisions, etc.Assist with project coordination meetings at Division, Department, State, and Federal levels, as applicable.Assist in the development of environmental documents and supporting technical documentation related to the NEPA process.Monitor environmental compliance through the life of the project and coordinate on-site project monitoring as needed.Assist in determining compensatory mitigation on a project if applicable.Additional Examples of Work Applicable to Water Quality Specialist:Assist the Department in compliance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits.Assist in the preparation and delivery of training on environmental stormwater regulations and best management practices to Department personnel.Conduct field testing and collection of water samples for various parameters.Minimum RequirementsEducation and experience: The educational equivalent to a master's degree from an accredited college or university in an environmental, biological, natural science, natural resources, or related field OR the educational equivalent to a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in an environmental, biological, natural science, natural resources, or related field plus two years' experience in an environmental science related field.Knowledge, skills and abilities: Knowledge of CWA and/or ESA permitting and compliance desired. Demonstrated proficient oral and written communication skills. Strong organizational skills and ability to manage diverse project assignments. Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret scientific data, technical procedures, and regulations. Proficiency in basic computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook.Physical requirements: Ability to traverse rugged terrain including, but not limited to, steep hills, creeks and streams, swamps, brush and timber covered property, fences, etc.Working conditions: Office and field environment with statewide travel, including overnight travel.Licenses, registrations and certifications: Valid driver's license.Additional Requirements Applicable to Water Quality Specialist:Working knowledge of NPDES stormwater permits and regulations under CWA Sections 401 and 402 preferred.("Accredited" means the educational institution or program is accredited by an accrediting organization recognized either by the United States Department of Education or by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation.)A criminal background check will be required to determine suitability of employment, and failure to meet these standards may cause the applicant to be rejected or terminated from that position.Equal Opportunity Employer This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
The Senior Environmental Scientist leads wetland and stream delineations, environmental permitting efforts, and natural resource assessments, while providing technical oversight and mentorship to junior staff. This role serves as a technical lead and client-facing point of contact on multidisciplinary environmental projects, managing project scope, schedule, and quality while supporting business development and agency relationships.

This role requires deep technical expertise, sound regulatory judgment, leadership capability, and a commitment to safety and quality.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership & Field Oversight

Lead and oversee wetland and stream delineations, ensuring compliance with USACE and applicable state methodologies
Serve as technical lead on complex or high-visibility environmental permitting projects
Review and approve field data, delineation reports, and technical documentation prepared by junior staff
Lead environmental site assessments, habitat assessments, and threatened & endangered species evaluations
Provide field oversight, training, and mentorship to Environmental Scientists and field crews
Resolve technical discrepancies and escalate complex regulatory issues appropriately

Regulatory & Agency Coordination

Lead preparation and submission of permit applications under Section 401/404 of the Clean Water Act and other applicable regulations
Serve as primary point of contact with regulatory agencies (USACE, EPA, state environmental agencies) on assigned projects
Interpret and apply evolving federal, state, and local environmental regulations to project strategy
Represent KERAMIDA in agency meetings, site visits, and public hearings as needed

Project & Client Management

Manage project scope, budget, schedule, and deliverable quality for assigned projects
Serve as a primary client contact, building and maintaining long-term client relationships
Support proposal development and business development efforts, including scoping and fee estimation
Mentor and develop junior staff, supporting their technical growth and career development
Complete timely and accurate time and expense reporting, and support project financial management

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Natural Resources, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred
Minimum 6-10 years of progressive experience in wetland delineation, environmental permitting, or natural resource consulting
Demonstrated experience leading Clean Water Act Section 401/404 permitting and agency coordination
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) certification or eligibility preferred
Proven experience managing project scope, budget, and staff
Proficiency with GIS/GPS software (e.g., ArcGIS, Trimble) and Microsoft Office
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record
Strong written, verbal, and client-facing communication skills
Demonstrated leadership, mentorship, and team management ability

Physical & Work Environment

Ability to work outdoors in varying and extreme weather conditions
Ability to navigate rough terrain, wetlands, and remote or undeveloped sites
Ability to bend, stoop, reach, and lift up to 40 pounds
Combination of fieldwork, client-facing engagement, and office-based project management
